# picreg

**Tuning-free variable selection with the Pivotal Information
Criterion.**

`picreg` fits sparse regression, classification and survival models with
the **Pivotal Information Criterion** (PIC) of [Sardy, van Cutsem and
van de Geer (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.04172). Like BIC or AIC,
PIC fixes its penalty level *before* looking at the response. Unlike
them, it fixes it at the **detection boundary**: the smallest penalty
that keeps pure noise out of the model with probability 1 - \alpha. This
penalty depends only on the design matrix, so PIC needs neither
cross-validation nor a grid of models, and it selects sparse,
interpretable models with a controlled number of false discoveries.

## Why PIC?

- **No tuning.** The regularization parameter is computed once from `X`,
  without cross-validation, validation set or path selection.
- **Calibrated false discoveries.** When the data carry no signal, PIC
  returns the empty model with probability 1 - \alpha (95% by default),
  for every family.
- **Sharp support recovery.** The probability of recovering exactly the
  true set of variables shows a phase transition, as in compressed
  sensing: close to one up to a critical sparsity level, then dropping.
- **Parsimony at no cost in prediction.** On benchmark datasets, PIC
  selects the smallest models among state-of-the-art selectors for a
  similar predictive performance ([see below](#performance)).
- **One interface, six models.** Gaussian, binomial, Poisson,
  exponential, Gumbel and Cox models, with the lasso, SCAD and MCP
  penalties, behind a `glmnet`-style API. The core is written in C++
  (RcppArmadillo).

## Installation

Install the released version from CRAN:

``` r

install.packages("picreg")
```

or the development version from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("VcMaxouuu/picreg")
```

## Quick start

`QuickStartExample` is a Gaussian dataset with n = 100 observations and
p = 30 predictors, of which only `gene_1`, …, `gene_5` carry signal.

``` r

library(picreg)

data(QuickStartExample)
X <- QuickStartExample$X
y <- QuickStartExample$y

fit <- pic(X, y, lambda_seed = 1)   # lambda_seed: reproducible calibration
summary(fit)
#> pic fit summary
#>   family    : gaussian
#>   penalty   : lasso
#>   lambda    : 0.3081
#>   dimensions: n = 100, p = 30
#>   selected  : 5 / 30
#>   intercept : 0.005989
#>
#>   Non-zero coefficients (original scale):
#>  variable coefficient
#>    gene_3     -0.7606
#>    gene_4     -0.6620
#>    gene_1     -0.4130
#>    gene_5      0.1495
#>    gene_2     -0.0571
```

The five active variables are recovered exactly, without any tuning. The
fit works with the usual methods:

``` r

coef(fit)                              # sparse coefficients, original scale
predict(fit, newx = X[1:3, ])          # predictions on new data
plot(fit)                              # lollipop plot of the selected effects
assess(fit, newx = X, newy = y,        # predictive and support-recovery metrics
       true_features = paste0("gene_", 1:5))
```

Changing the model or the penalty only takes an argument; the
calibration can be reused across penalties, since it does not depend on
them:

``` r

fit_scad <- pic(X, y, penalty = "scad", lambda = fit$lambda_pdb)

data(BinomialExample)
fit_logit <- pic(BinomialExample$X, BinomialExample$y, family = "binomial")

data(CoxExample)
fit_cox <- pic(CoxExample$X, CoxExample$y, family = "cox")
```

## Supported models

| Model | `family =` | Response `y` | Loss minimized by PIC |
|----|----|----|----|
| Linear regression | `"gaussian"` | numeric | square root of the mean squared error (square-root lasso) |
| Logistic regression | `"binomial"` | 0/1, logical, or two-level factor | weighted score loss |
| Poisson regression | `"poisson"` | non-negative counts | weighted score loss |
| Exponential regression | `"exponential"` | non-negative | negative log-likelihood |
| Gumbel location-scale | `"gumbel"` | numeric | exponential of the negative log-likelihood, scale profiled out |
| Cox proportional hazards | `"cox"` | `(time, event)` matrix or [`survival::Surv`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/survival/man/Surv.html) | square root of the negative log partial likelihood (Breslow ties) |

Each model is combined with one of three penalties: `"lasso"` (\ell_1),
`"scad"` or `"mcp"`. The non-convex penalties reduce the shrinkage bias
of the lasso on large coefficients and recover the support at higher
sparsity levels.

## How PIC chooses the penalty

PIC minimizes

\phi\Bigl(l_n\bigl(g(\beta_0\mathbf{1} +
X\boldsymbol\beta)\bigr)\Bigr) + \lambda\_\alpha^{\mathrm{PDB}}\\
\mathrm{pen}(\boldsymbol\beta),

where l_n is a base loss and (\phi, g) are model-specific
transformations. The origin \boldsymbol\beta = \mathbf 0 is a solution
as soon as the penalty exceeds \Lambda, the sup-norm of the gradient of
the loss at the null fit. PIC sets the penalty at the **pivotal
detection boundary** \lambda\_\alpha^{\mathrm{PDB}}, the (1 -
\alpha)-quantile of \Lambda under pure noise. The transformations (\phi,
g) are chosen so that this quantile does not depend on the unknown
intercept or scale: it can be computed from `X` alone, before the model
is fitted.

[`pic()`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/pic.md) computes
\lambda\_\alpha^{\mathrm{PDB}} with one of three methods, through
`lambda_method`:

| Method | Principle | When to use |
|----|----|----|
| `"mc_exact"` (default) | Monte Carlo under the null model of the family | small to moderate problems |
| `"mc_gaussian"` | Monte Carlo under the Gaussian limit of the gradient | large n |
| `"analytical"` | closed-form Bonferroni bound, conservative | very large problems |

``` r

pdb_summary(fit)        # calibration details and simulated null distribution
plot(fit$lambda_pdb)    # null distribution with the selected lambda
```

## Performance

The results below are reported in [Sardy, van Cutsem and van de Geer
(2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.04172), and the scripts that produce
them are in
[`simulations/`](https://github.com/VcMaxouuu/picreg/tree/main/simulations).

**Calibration under pure noise.** On Gaussian data with n = p = 100 and
no signal, PIC selected at least one variable in 4% of the datasets, for
a target of \alpha = 5\\. Cross-validated lasso (`cv.glmnet`,
`lambda.min`) did so in 43% of the datasets, EBIC in 22% and BIC in 96%.

**Phase transition.** Probability of exact support recovery as a
function of the number s of active variables (Gaussian model, n = p =
100, non-zero coefficients of magnitude 3 with random signs, 100
replications per s):

![Probability of exact support recovery against sparsity for picreg and
cv.glmnet](reference/figures/README-phase-transition.png)

**Real data.** Mean test performance (mean model size in parentheses)
over 100 random 70/30 train-test splits (90 for Riboflavin), after an
unpenalized refit on the selected variables. BIC and EBIC use forward
selection.

| Dataset | n | p | PIC (lasso) | PIC (SCAD) | cv.glmnet | BIC | EBIC |
|----|---:|---:|----|----|----|----|----|
| *Regression, relative test MSE* |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Prostate cancer | 97 | 8 | **0.435** (3.1) | 0.456 (2.7) | 0.451 (5.9) | 0.454 (3.1) | 0.460 (2.8) |
| Diabetes | 442 | 64 | 0.531 (4.6) | 0.535 (4.7) | 0.536 (17.6) | **0.529** (6.3) | 0.542 (4.7) |
| Riboflavin | 71 | 4088 | **0.411** (6.0) | **0.411** (6.0) | 1.323 (37.5) | 0.754 (40.0) | 0.492 (8.0) |
| *Classification, test accuracy* |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Breast cancer | 569 | 30 | **0.965** (4.5) | 0.950 (3.0) | 0.963 (12.9) | 0.962 (5.2) | 0.963 (4.3) |
| Ionosphere | 351 | 33 | 0.872 (4.6) | 0.867 (4.3) | **0.878** (17.5) | 0.867 (8.0) | 0.864 (6.0) |
| Sonar | 208 | 60 | 0.715 (4.0) | 0.720 (3.3) | **0.735** (19.8) | 0.729 (7.6) | 0.722 (4.4) |

On every dataset, a PIC fit selects the smallest model, with a
predictive performance close to the best one.

## Main functions

| Task | Functions |
|----|----|
| Fit a model | [`pic()`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/pic.md) |
| Inspect a fit | [`summary()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/summary.html), [`coef()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/coef.html), [`plot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html) |
| Predict and evaluate | [`predict()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/predict.html), [`assess()`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/assess.md) |
| Penalty calibration | [`lambda_pdb()`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/lambda_pdb.md), [`pdb_summary()`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/pdb_summary.md), `plot(fit$lambda_pdb)` |
| Survival analysis | `predict(type = "survival")`, [`feature_effects_on_survival()`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/feature_effects_on_survival.md), [`plot_survival_curves()`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/plot_survival_curves.md), [`plot_baseline()`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/plot_baseline.md), [`concordance_index()`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/concordance_index.md) |
| Diagnostics | [`phase_transition()`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/phase_transition.md), [`pdb_asymptotic()`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/pdb_asymptotic.md) |

# Package index

## Model fitting

The single high-level entry point.

- [`pic()`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/pic.md) :
  Sparse linear regression using the Pivotal Information Criterion.

## Methods for fitted models

S3 methods shared across all families.

- [`summary(`*`<pic>`*`)`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/summary.pic.md)
  : Summarize a fitted pic model.

- [`coef(`*`<pic>`*`)`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/coef.pic.md)
  : Coefficients of a fitted pic model.

- [`predict(`*`<pic>`*`)`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/predict.pic.md)
  : Linear predictor / response prediction for a pic fit.

- [`plot(`*`<pic>`*`)`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/plot.pic.md)
  : Horizontal lollipop plot of the non-zero coefficients of a pic fit.

- [`assess()`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/assess.md) :

  Assess performance of a `pic` fit.

## Families and penalties

- [`pic_families`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/pic_families.md)
  : GLM families for pic — descriptor layer.
- [`pic_penalties`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/pic_penalties.md)
  : Sparsity-inducing penalties for pic.

## Choosing the penalty level

The Pivotal Detection Boundary selector and its diagnostics.

- [`lambda_pdb()`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/lambda_pdb.md)
  : Pivotal Detection Boundary regularization selector
- [`pdb_summary()`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/pdb_summary.md)
  : Summary of the PDB lambda selector.
- [`pdb_asymptotic()`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/pdb_asymptotic.md)
  : Asymptotic behavior of the PDB null distribution.
- [`plot(`*`<pic.lambda_pdb>`*`)`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/plot.pic.lambda_pdb.md)
  : Plot the PDB null distribution.
- [`plot(`*`<pic.pdb_asymptotic>`*`)`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/plot.pic.pdb_asymptotic.md)
  : Plot of the PDB asymptotic behavior.

## Variable-selection diagnostics

- [`phase_transition()`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/phase_transition.md)
  : Phase-transition analysis of support recovery.

- [`plot(`*`<pic.phase_transition>`*`)`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/plot.pic.phase_transition.md)
  :

  Phase-transition plot for a `pic.phase_transition` object.

## Survival utilities

Helpers for the Cox proportional-hazards family.

- [`feature_effects_on_survival()`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/feature_effects_on_survival.md)
  : Effect of one feature on the Cox survival curve.

- [`plot_baseline()`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/plot_baseline.md)
  : Plot Cox baseline cumulative hazard and baseline survival.

- [`plot_survival_curves()`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/plot_survival_curves.md)
  : Plot subject-specific Cox survival curves.

- [`baseline_functions()`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/baseline_functions.md)
  : Breslow baseline cumulative hazard and survival.

- [`concordance_index()`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/concordance_index.md)
  : Harrell's concordance index.

- [`cox_partial_log_likelihood()`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/cox_partial_log_likelihood.md)
  :

  Breslow partial log-likelihood (negative, normalized by `n`).

## Datasets

- [`QuickStartExample`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/QuickStartExample.md)
  : Small Gaussian dataset for the introductory vignette.
- [`BinomialExample`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/BinomialExample.md)
  : Small binary-classification dataset for the Binomial section of the
  vignette.
- [`CoxExample`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/CoxExample.md)
  : Small survival dataset for the Cox section of the vignette.

## Internal

Overview pages and print methods.

- [`pic_methods`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/pic_methods.md)
  : S3 methods for fitted pic objects.

- [`pic_plots`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/pic_plots.md)
  : Plot methods for pic fits and diagnostics.

- [`pic_survival`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/pic_survival.md)
  : Survival utilities for the Cox family.

- [`print(`*`<pic.family>`*`)`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/print.pic.family.md)
  : Pretty-print a pic family descriptor.

- [`print(`*`<pic.pdb_asymptotic>`*`)`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/print.pic.pdb_asymptotic.md)
  : Print PDB asymptotic diagnostic.

- [`print(`*`<pic.phase_transition>`*`)`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/print.pic.phase_transition.md)
  : Print phase-transition analysis.

- [`print(`*`<summary.pic>`*`)`](https://vcmaxouuu.github.io/picreg/reference/print.summary.pic.md)
  :

  Print a `summary.pic` object.
